content:
acme-app-Team: hey @Maya – we're seeing a lot of 429s and long tail latency during short bursts from our integration tests. looks like requests queue up for a second then start failing. can you help?

Maya (support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a curl or a short repro? also any response headers you saw? 429s can be rate-limit or quota.

acme-app-Team: here's the minimal repro: we run 300 parallel connections for ~10s each. majority of reqs return quickly but ~15% get 429 + long latency before the 429. example response headers: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit: 120/min
x-rw-rate-remaining: 0
x-rw-retry-after: 4
x-rw-kv-cache: miss
x-rw-batch-id: 0x7f3b2
content-type: application/json

{"error":"quota_exceeded", "detail": "concurrent capacity exhausted"}
```

Maya (support): thanks — the x-rw-kv-cache header is useful. I see a lot of "miss" there which will increase per-request work. Did you warm the prefix cache or use consistent prompts?

acme-app-Team: our traffic is bursty and mostly different prompts. we thought continuous batching + KV cache would handle it. we have batch_window_ms=5 and continuous_batching=true.

Alex (sre): tagging @Eli from eng-runtime — this looks like perceived throttling when cold KV cache + batching wait times cause bursts to compress and exceed per-GPU inflight token limits.

Eli (eng-runtime): plausible. quick explainer: continuous batching batches within batch_window_ms to increase GPU throughput, but if many unique prefixes hit the KV cache cold, each request does extra memory ops and increases per-request latency. When lots of requests arrive at once, the runtime will open many inflight streams to fill batches which can hit per-device concurrency caps and trigger quota/429 enforcement. result = some requests delayed, others 429'd.

Jing (infra): we also have a short burst quota to protect multi-tenant capacity. those 429s with x-rw-rate-remaining:0 indicate you exhausted your per-minute burst allowance. that can be hit faster when batching compresses upstream traffic.

acme-app-Team: ok. any mitigation steps on our side besides smoothing the load? this is a test suite we can't easily slow down too much.

Maya (support): short-term: add jittered backoff on 429 with exponential backoff + jitter; reduce client-level concurrency (e.g., from 300 -> 80) and use a small rate limiter to ramp into bursts. also set a Retry-After handler to respect x-rw-retry-after.

Eli (eng-runtime): additional suggestions: 
- prime the KV cache for common prefixes (send low-cost warmup requests before the burst).
- set batch_window_ms slightly higher (10-20ms) to let batching absorb spike variance; this can reduce instantaneous inflight streams.
- enable per-route cache hints if you can mark prompts likely to be repeated.

acme-app-Team: curious — you recommended increasing batch_window_ms. won't that increase latency for single requests?

Eli (eng-runtime): small increases (10-20ms) typically trade a tiny median latency for much better throughput and fewer inflight workers, which reduces chance of hitting concurrency caps. Since your workload is bursty and mostly high QPS during tests, the throughput gain usually wins.

Alex (sre): from infra side we can temporarily raise the per-tenant burst quota while you run tests. but we prefer you use client-side smoothing because global fairness matters.

acme-app-Team: that would help for now. can you also check if any retries from our SDK caused a feedback loop? we do automatic retries on 5xx and 429.

Maya (support): please send logs showing retry timings. a common pattern is tight retry loops that amplify bursts. also include the request signature (first 80 chars of prompt) so we can correlate with KV hits.

acme-app-Team: pasted a small sample: 

```
// simplified node snippet
const p = []
for (let i=0; i<300; i++) {
  p.push(fetch(api, { body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: `order-${i}` }) }))
}
await Promise.all(p)
// we have exponential retry with base 100ms, multiplier 1.8, max 3 retries
```

Maya (support): that pattern will definitely produce retry storms if many requests fail at once. reduce parallelism or add a central queue with token bucket to pace outgoing requests in the test harness.

Eli (eng-runtime): I'll look at trace logs if you can give an example trace-id from a failing request. runtime traces show KV hit/miss and batch composition.

acme-app-Team: here's a trace id from a 429: t-9f2b6a8d. also a few request ids: r-3344, r-3347.

Eli (eng-runtime): got them — thanks. I can see the sequence: many requests in same 20ms window, KV cache miss for most, runtime created 12 small batches across 3 GPUs, per-GPU inflight > limit for ~2s, and our quota gate fired which returned 429 for the last requests in the window.

Eli (eng-runtime): proposed runtime-side fixes: 
- track short-term burst smoothing: if inflight > threshold, temporarily delay accepts by a few ms to let batches absorb.
- per-client adaptive queueing that respects recent KV miss rate.
- add a hint header for "x-client-warmup" to prefer slower ramp-up policies (we can discuss exposure).

Alex (sre): we can escalate to a short-lived quota bump for acme-app-Team for tomorrow's test run. sending request to quota team now.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued — quota bump request id qb-2026-77 submitted.

acme-app-Team: thanks. in parallel we'll: 
- reduce test concurrency to 80 and run with backoff, and try batch_window_ms=12ms and kv warmups.
- add a small pre-warm phase that does 50 warmup requests for most prefixes.

Maya (support): sounds good. follow-ups: please upload a short repro script and the raw response headers to the ticket. I'll keep thread open until we've validated the warmup + quota bump solves it. :thumbsup:

acme-app-Team: quick question — does KV cache report 'hit' for repeated prompts inside the same batch? we saw hit/miss mixed for similar prompts.

Eli (eng-runtime): if the same prefix appears multiple times in the same batch and the KV entries are fetched early enough, subsequent entries in that same batch can be served from the in-batch cache. however race conditions exist if the fetch is still in-flight, so you'll see mixed hit/miss occasionally. warming across multiple seconds is more reliable.

Jing (infra): logged infra ticket INF-8721 to monitor cross-tenant burst signals and consider adaptive quota heuristics.

Maya (support): summary action items: 
- acme-app-Team: reduce parallelism, add jittered backoff, add warmup requests, try batch_window_ms=12-20ms, re-run tests.
- SRE/Infra: temporary quota bump qb-2026-77 applied for tomorrow window; monitor.
- Eng-runtime: follow up on adaptive delay + hint header.

acme-app-Team: will do. thanks everyone — we'll report back with test results and the repro script.

Maya (support): thanks — keeping this thread open. if anything changes, ping me.
